title: Cambridge Primary Mathematics Curriculum Framework (0096)
version: Version 1.1; published September 2020 for first teaching September 2021
notes: Teks diambil langsung dari salinan PDF resmi Cambridge (nama berkas asli Cambridge: ...0096_tcm142-592530.pdf) yang dicerminkan di cmapspublic2.ihmc.us; PDF resmi di School Support Hub memerlukan login.
Kode = nomor stage + kode sub-strand + nomor urut (mis. 1Nc.05). TWM.01-08 berlaku untuk semua stage 1-6; teksnya adalah definisi karakteristik dari tabel di hlm. 9.
Sub-butir (o) dalam dokumen asli digabung ke dalam satu baris dipisah ';'.

entries.text: Specialising: Choosing an example and checking to see if it satisfies or does not satisfy specific mathematical criteria
Generalising: Recognising an underlying pattern by identifying many examples that satisfy the same mathematical criteria
Conjecturing: Forming mathematical questions or ideas
Convincing: Presenting evidence to justify or challenge a mathematical idea or solution
Characterising: Identifying and describing the mathematical properties of an object
Classifying: Organising objects into groups according to their mathematical properties
Critiquing: Comparing and evaluating mathematical ideas, representations or solutions to identify advantages and disadvantages
Improving: Refining mathematical ideas or representations to develop a more effective approach or solution
Count objects from 0 to 20, recognising conservation of number and one-to-one correspondence.
Recognise the number of objects presented in familiar patterns up to 10, without counting.
Estimate the number of objects or people (up to 20), and check by counting.
Count on in ones, twos or tens, and count back in ones and tens, starting from any number (from 0 to 20).
Understand even and odd numbers as ‘every other number’ when counting (from 0 to 20).
Use familiar language to describe sequences of objects.
Recite, read and write number names and whole numbers (from 0 to 20).
Understand addition as: counting on; combining two sets.
Understand subtraction as: counting back; take away; difference.
Recognise complements of 10.
Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers (where the answer is from 0 to 20).
Know doubles up to double 10.
Recognise money used in local currency.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Understand that zero represents none of something.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Compose, decompose and regroup numbers from 10 to 20.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Understand the relative size of quantities to compare and order numbers from 0 to 20.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Recognise and use ordinal numbers from 1st to 10th.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that an object or shape can be split into two equal parts or two unequal parts.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that a half can describe one of two equal parts of a quantity or set of objects.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that a half can act as an operator (whole number answers).

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand and visualise that halves can be combined to make wholes.
Use familiar language to describe units of time.
Know the days of the week and the months of the year.
Recognise time to the hour and half hour.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify, describe and sort 2D shapes by their characteristics or properties, including reference to number of sides and whether the sides are curved or straight.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Use familiar language to describe length, including long, longer, longest, thin, thinner, thinnest, short, shorter, shortest, tall, taller and tallest.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify, describe and sort 3D shapes by their properties, including reference to the number of faces, edges and whether faces are flat or curved.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Use familiar language to describe mass, including heavy, light, less and more.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Use familiar language to describe capacity, including full, empty, less and more.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Differentiate between 2D and 3D shapes.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify when a shape looks identical as it rotates.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Explore instruments that have numbered scales, and select the most appropriate instrument to measure length, mass, capacity and temperature.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Position and transformation
entries.text: Use familiar language to describe position and direction.
Answer non-statistical questions (categorical data).
Record, organise and represent categorical data using: practical resources and drawings; lists and tables; Venn and Carroll diagrams; block graphs and pictograms.
Describe data, using familiar language including reference to more, less, most or least to answer non- statistical questions and discuss conclusions.
Count objects from 0 to 100.
Recognise the number of objects presented in unfamiliar patterns up to 10, without counting.
Estimate the number of objects or people (up to 100).
Count on and count back in ones, twos, fives or tens, starting from any number (from 0 to 100).
Recognise the characteristics of even and odd numbers (from 0 to 100).
Recognise, describe and extend numerical sequences (from 0 to 100).
Recite, read and write number names and whole numbers (from 0 to 100).
Understand and explain the relationship between addition and subtraction.
Recognise complements of 20 and complements of multiples of 10 (up to 100).
Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers with up to two digits (no regrouping of ones or tens).
Understand multiplication as: repeated addition; an array.
Understand division as: sharing (number of items per group); grouping (number of groups).
Know 1, 2, 5 and 10 times tables.
Recognise value and money notation used in local currency.
Compare values of different combinations of coins or notes.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Understand and explain that the value of each digit in a 2-digit number is determined by its position in that number, recognising zero as a place holder.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Compose, decompose and regroup 2-digit numbers, using tens and ones.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Understand the relative size of quantities to compare and order 2-digit numbers.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Recognise and use ordinal numbers.

entries.strand: Number: Place value, ordering and rounding
entries.text: Round 2-digit numbers to the nearest 10.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that an object or shape can be split into four equal parts or four unequal parts.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that a quarter can describe one of four equal parts of a quantity or set of objects.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that one half and one quarter can be interpreted as division.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand that fractions (half, quarter and three-quarters) can act as operators.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Recognise the relative size of 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 1, and the equivalence of 1/2 and 2/4, and 2/2, 4/4 and 1.

entries.strand: Number: Fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion
entries.text: Understand and visualise that wholes, halves and quarters can be combined to create new fractions.
Order and compare units of time (seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years).
Read and record time to five minutes in digital notation (12-hour) and on analogue clocks.
Interpret and use the information in calendars.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify, describe, sort, name and sketch 2D shapes by their properties, including reference to regular polygons, number of sides and vertices. Recognise these shapes in different positions and orientations.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Understand that a circle has a centre and any point on the boundary is at the same distance from the centre.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Understand that length is a fixed distance between two points. Estimate and measure lengths using non-standard or standard units.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Draw and measure lines, using standard units.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify, describe, sort and name 3D shapes by their properties, including reference to number and shapes of faces, edges and vertices.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Understand that mass is the quantity of matter in an object. Estimate and measure familiar objects using non-standard or standard units.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Understand that capacity is the maximum amount that an object can contain. Estimate and measure the capacity of familiar objects using non-standard or standard units.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify 2D and 3D shapes in familiar objects.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Identify a horizontal or vertical line of symmetry on 2D shapes and patterns.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Predict and check how many times a shape looks identical as it completes a full turn.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Understand that an angle is a description of a turn, including reference to the terms whole, half and quarter turns, both clockwise and anticlockwise.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Geometrical reasoning, shapes and measurements
entries.text: Understand a measuring scale as a continuous number line where intermediate points have value.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Position and transformation
entries.text: Use knowledge of position and direction to describe movement.

entries.strand: Geometry and Measure: Position and transformation
entries.text: Sketch the reflection of a 2D shape in a vertical mirror line, including where the mirror line is the edge of the shape.
Conduct an investigation to answer non-statistical and statistical questions (categorical data).

Record, organise and represent categorical data. Choose and explain which representation to use in a given situation: lists and tables; Venn and Carroll diagrams; tally charts; block graphs and pictograms.
Describe data, identifying similarities and variations to answer non-statistical and statistical questions and discuss conclusions.
Use familiar language associated with patterns and randomness, including regular pattern and random pattern.
Conduct chance experiments with two outcomes, and present and describe the results.
